nodes.label: Docker Compose Services
nodes.rationale: Docker Compose deployment — including automated Let's Encrypt bootstrapping via cert-bootstrap and self-reloading nginx — was not in the original plan, which treated Docker as future work. It shipped as the actual deployment mechanism instead.

nodes.label: CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The knip dead-code check runs as a non-blocking (continue-on-error) step because its false-positive-avoidance config in knip.json is new and unproven; it is meant to flip to a hard failure once it runs clean for a while with no new false-positive categories appearing.

nodes.label: UserTenant
nodes.rationale: Multi-tenancy means one account needs to represent different people-in-context at different schools; a column on User can't express 'TEACHER here, PARENT there' for one person, so the UserTenant join table (user, school, role) makes that possible — it's why almost every entity in the domain model carries an explicit tenant reference.

nodes.label: StudentFee
nodes.rationale: Discounts are implemented as first-class (StudentFee.discount_amount) rather than deferred — the original plan flagged discounts/scholarships as a future gap, but they shipped as part of the core model instead and factor directly into every due/balance calculation.

nodes.label: Multi-Tenancy
nodes.rationale: Biddaloy hosts many independent schools on one deployment; School rows are tenants and everything school-specific is scoped to exactly one tenant, but a single User account is not tenant-scoped since one person can belong to multiple schools with a different role at each.

nodes.label: CSRF Posture
nodes.rationale: Bearer-authenticated routes need no CSRF handling since browsers never auto-attach the Authorization header to a cross-site request. Only the two cookie-authenticated routes (refresh, logout) carry an ambient credential, so they're layered with SameSite=Strict, SameOriginGuard, and the __Host- cookie prefix instead of blanket CSRF middleware everywhere.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Rotation & Reuse Detection
nodes.rationale: Using an already-used refresh token is treated as theft — the entire token family is revoked and a TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED audit row is written — unless it falls within a 10-second grace window of its own rotation, which is treated as two concurrent requests racing rather than an attack.

nodes.label: Access Token Denylist
nodes.rationale: A Redis key per jti with TTL matching the access token's own lifetime is viable specifically because access tokens are already short-lived (15 min) — this is not a full blacklist of every issued token.

nodes.label: Login Brute-Force Protection
nodes.rationale: Per-IP rate limiting, per-identifier lockout (5 fails/15 min), and progressive delay are combined with an identical response path whether or not the account exists (bcrypt.compare always runs, even against a dummy hash) specifically so there is no timing or content signal an attacker could use to enumerate valid accounts.

nodes.label: Column-Level Encryption (Deferred)
nodes.rationale: Evaluated but deliberately deferred: column-level encryption would break exact-match login lookups and range/LIKE searches the app depends on, and would not protect against a credentialed attacker who can just query the API — that is an access-control problem, not a storage-encryption one. Revisit only if a regulatory requirement forces it, or KMS-backed searchable/blind-index encryption becomes practical.

nodes.label: CommunicationProvider Adapter Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every channel implements the same CommunicationProvider interface so the controller/service layer never branches on medium — it asks the registry for whatever handles the medium for the tenant and calls .send(). Per-tenant provider config lives in School.settings, so different schools can use different providers without any code change.

nodes.label: SMS Channel (Greenweb / Mim SMS)
nodes.rationale: The original plan specified Twilio for SMS/WhatsApp. What shipped instead is Bangladesh-market-specific: Greenweb SMS and Mim SMS gateways, selected per-tenant via sms-provider.factory.ts.

nodes.label: Component Boundary Rule (ESLint)
nodes.rationale: client-admin and client-student may only import from @biddaloy/ui's published subpaths, never Radix directly or a deep ui/src path — enforced by a custom ESLint rule so a boundary violation fails CI instead of relying on convention.

nodes.label: Financial-Mutation Guard (ESLint)
nodes.rationale: Blocks optimistic UI on any useMutation touching a payment or enrollment endpoint: showing '৳4,500 received' and then rolling back on error means the UI confirmed a payment that didn't happen — at a cash counter, with the parent standing there, that's not a glitch, it's an argument. Enforced as a lint rule so it's caught every time a mutation is added or edited, not just when someone remembers to check in review.

nodes.label: TanStack Router (file-based routing)
nodes.rationale: Chosen specifically for typed, per-route search-param validation: a route declares a Zod validateSearch schema with .catch() fallbacks, so a malformed query param degrades to a sensible default instead of crashing the page.

nodes.label: API Documentation (Swagger)
nodes.rationale: In production the /api/docs route is off by default (a real 404) unless ENABLE_API_DOCS=true, and setting that without both Basic Auth credentials refuses to boot — loud failure over a silently unauthenticated docs route.

nodes.label: knip Dead-Code Detection
nodes.rationale: server/ is deliberately excluded from knip (ignoreWorkspaces in knip.json) because NestJS decorators, TypeORM migrations loaded via glob, and CLI scripts produce too many false positives for knip's default static-analysis heuristics to be useful there without dedicated config.

nodes.label: Documentation Style Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Any documentation in the repo must be dead simple to understand: prefer a Mermaid diagram over a paragraph whenever describing a flow or relationship, include a concrete example wherever an abstract description would leave the reader guessing, write for someone not already an expert, and keep the honest 'why' including deviations from any prior plan.

nodes.label: RTK (Rust Token Killer)
nodes.rationale: A token-optimized CLI proxy: prefixing shell commands with rtk applies dedicated output filters where available (git, tests, builds, package managers) and passes through unchanged otherwise, cutting token usage 60-90% on common development operations.
